subject: Clarify context anchoring and rounding — implications for discount structure
messages:
From: Elise Ramirez <elise@cloudfirstretail.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procure@cloudfirstretail.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T15:12:00Z
Subject: Context anchoring: billing unit granularity and discount impact

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks for the proposal you sent last week. Procurement had a couple of follow-ups before we escalate to budget approval:

- How do you meter "long context" interactions vs normal requests? For our retail agent, typical sessions include a 8–12k prefix plus frequent 2–4k follow-ups.
- Do KV/prefix cache hits reduce billable tokens (or is the whole context recharged on every call)?
- How does rounding/minimums work for streaming responses vs single-call generation? We need to quantify worst-case invoice numbers to justify the commitment.

Also: the discount tiers in the proposal are based on naive per-token consumption. If long contexts are counted fully every call, the effective committed tokens blow past our projected usage. Can you confirm the exact billing unit and rounding quantum so we can model spend?

If useful, I can share a week of anonymized session traces. Hoping to finalize numbers quickly — procurement is targeting a decision by EOD next Wednesday.

Best,
Elise Ramirez
Director, AI Platform
CloudFirst Retail

---
Attachment: sample_session_traces.csv (referenced)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Elise Ramirez <elise@cloudfirstretail.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-25T17:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Context anchoring: billing unit granularity and discount impact

Hi Elise — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front, then a proposal for how we model this for CloudFirst: 

1) Token accounting: billable tokens = prompt tokens + generated tokens after our tokenizer. KV/prefix caching reduces the prompt portion that is recomputed: if the prefix is served from KV cache with a hit, the prompt tokens for that part are not recharged per request.

2) Long contexts: we offer two billing models in practice: per-token (default) and session-amortized (optional for committed customers). Per-token charges apply to the effective token delta per call; session-amortized treats a pinned context as amortized across N calls for commitment math.

3) Rounding/minimums: billing is quantized to 1,000-token increments for per-token SKUs (we round up). Streaming responses are counted the same as single-call generation for billable tokens; the streaming buffer does not create a separate bucket.

Given CloudFirst's usage pattern, my recommendation is one of three options (attached: pricing_proposal_v2.pdf):

- Option A: Per-token with a 1k quantum, standard volume discounts. Simple, but with long prefixes you may see higher look-ahead spikes.
- Option B: Session-amortized commit. We charge a guaranteed monthly token floor and amortize prefix cost over a configured number of sessions (e.g., 30k tokens prefix amortized across 100k sessions for discount tier calculation). Rounding still applies to per-call meter, but the commit math uses amortized consumption.
- Option C: Hybrid seat + overage — seats include a fixed monthly token band sized for your base traffic; overages charged per-token with 1k quantum. We can attach a long-context premium discount if you enable KV cache and prefix persistence.

Next steps: Grace and Ben are cc'd — can you share the week of traces? Grace will produce a worked example showing invoice impact and rounding effects. If that looks reasonable, Ben can propose the commercial concessions we can extend for a commit. I can get a DocuSign to you after we agree on the model.

Would you be available for a 30-min call tomorrow at 10am PT?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Sales Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pricing_proposal_v2.pdf
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-26T09:30:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Context anchoring: billing unit granularity and discount impact — rounding examples

Vanessa / Ben — I ran CloudFirst's example traces (Elise's file) through our billing sim and produced two concise worked samples (attached: rounding_examples.csv). Highlights: 

- Baseline pattern: 9k prefix + 3k interaction average, 50k calls/day (typical of their agent).

Worked Example 1 — Per-token, 1k quantum (round up):
- Average per-call billable tokens before rounding: 12,000 tokens
- Rounded billable tokens per call: 12,000 (already multiple of 1k)
- Daily billable tokens: 12,000 * 50,000 = 600,000,000 tokens
- Monthly (30d): 18,000,000,000 tokens

Worked Example 2 — Per-token with prefix cached hit rate 60% (prefix excluded from per-call billable tokens when hit):
- Effective prompt reduction: 9k * 60% = 5,400 tokens saved on average
- Average per-call billable tokens: 6,600 tokens (rounded up to 7,000 due to 1k quantum)
- Daily billable tokens: 7,000 * 50,000 = 350,000,000 tokens (brings monthly down to ~10.5B)

Key point: rounding to 1k interacts with cache hit rates nonlinearly — even modest cache hits move you multiple tiers when monthly commitments are near thresholds. The attached CSV includes tier-breach sensitivity (i.e., how much cache hit rate must improve to drop a tier).

Commercial recommendation for negotiation: if CloudFirst enables prefix persistence + warms the KV cache to sustain >=50% hit rate, offer:
- A 12% volume discount off list for first 12 months,
- Plus a 0.75x adjustment factor for long-prefix tokens when calculating discount-qualification consumption (i.e., long-prefix tokens count as 0.75 tokens for the purposes of hitting tier thresholds) — only if prefix hit rate verification is enabled in the console (we can audit).

I also recommend explicitly capping the monthly rounding tail exposure with a monthly floor credit equal to the 95th percentile of rounding waste in the sample month. That makes procurement comfortable with the unknowns.

Happy to walk through the CSV on the call.

Grace
Director, Pricing & Revenue Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachment: rounding_examples.csv
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-04-26T12:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Context anchoring: billing unit granularity and discount impact — commercial ask

Quick summary for procurement:

- Approve Option B (session-amortized commit) or Option C (hybrid seat) — both reduce invoice variance.
- Offer: 10% introductory discount on committed band, plus the 0.75x prefix-adjustment for tier calculation (conditional on enabling and auditing KV hits).
- Cap rounding exposure: provide a monthly rounding-credit equal to the 95th percentile of rounding overhead from the first month of the pilot.

If leadership approves the above, I will sign off on a commercial memo and we can issue a DocuSign with the amended terms (I will include the cap and the conditional audit clause). Vanessa — if you and Elise align on Option B, I recommend we pre-authorize a 30-day pilot at 50% of the requested commit to validate hit rates; then convert to the full commit on meeting the threshold.

Ben
Head of Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
